countGroup.Name_As_Printed: Mr. W. J. F. Donald Co.C., chairman of the County Antrim Education Committee

source.title: Larne Times, 11 September 1952, p. 6 ("Education Minister's appeal at Islandmagee ceremony"); Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1952, p. 10 ("Nominations for county and rural councils: no contests for Antrim County Council"); Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1949, p. 7; Belfast Telegraph, 6 June 1952, p. 6 ("Notice of Result of Elections: County of Antrim, election of county councillors, 1952")
source.publisher: Larne Times (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: no nomination was received for the division and the retiring member continued (Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1952, p. 10); named as a sitting member of the new council early in the term (Larne Times, 11 September 1952, p. 6: the Minister 'was greeted by Mr. W. J. F. Donald Co.C., chairman of the County Antrim Education Committee', who presided)

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council; nominations received on 20 May 1952, withdrawals to 21 May, and polling, where necessary, on Thursday 5 June 1952 ('polling day will be Thursday, June 5', Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1952, p. 10). There was no contest in any Antrim division, so no poll was held in the county. No party labels were printed. The returning officer's notice of result (Belfast Telegraph, 6 June 1952, p. 6) lists each division with its candidate, and the retiring members deemed re-elected where there was no nomination (Ballyclare and Glenarm). division inferred from the 2 June 1949 return (W. J. F. Donald; Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1949, p. 7); the Larne Times, 11 September 1952, p. 6 names the member as sitting for the new council (opening of the Mullaghdubh (Islandmagee) school extension by the Minister of Education, September 1952). Styled County Councillor and chairman of the county's Education Committee three months into the term. The 1952 list does not print Glenarm; he held it from 1949 (no nomination, retiring member retained the seat) and was renominated in 1955. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
